## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 10 (titled *Saṅghabheda*) is the tenth disciplinary rule in the *saṅghādisesa* class for monks in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule provides that a monk who endeavors to create a schism in the monastic Order is subject to formal suspension [SuttaCentral]. Its origin story (*nidāna*) relates the account of the Buddha's cousin Devadatta attempting to fracture the Saṅgha [SuttaCentral]. In modern studies on Pali citation systems, this rule (abbreviated *Sanghad. 10*) has been cited to illustrate issues in canonical paragraph numbering across different editions [Kingsbury 2002]. SuttaCentral lists five translations across five languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Full parallels to this rule are preserved across the monastic codes of various Buddhist lineages, including the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Pātimokkhas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, and Mahāsaṅghika traditions in Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese, as well as the Pali *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Saṅghādisesa 14) and the *Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Both SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus identify an extensive passage-level parallel and internal text reuse with the *Saṁghabhedakakkhandhaka* (Kd 17), with DharmaNexus finding 58 shared passages totaling over 17,000 matching characters (longest segment §1.1.2–1.2.9 aligned with Kd 17 §3.14.1–3.15.6) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records extensive Pali-internal overlap with related disciplinary procedures in *Saṅghādisesa* 11, 12, and 13, the *Kammakkhandhaka* (Kd 11), *Cīvarakkhandhaka* (Kd 8), and later Vinaya exegetical treatises such as the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language automated alignments further link the text to the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001 / D0001-3), and commentarial works like the Tibetan *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104) [DharmaNexus].
